messages:
Amy: Heads-up — noticed a sharp p99 per-token latency spike in eu-west-1 around 06:14 UTC. p95 stayed ~120ms but p99 jumped to ~850ms for ~20m. tokens/sec for the affected shards dropped ~30%. Could be sampling noise but worth a quick look.
Sanjay: I saw that too from the synthetic client traces. Do we have any concurrent GPU scheduling/backpressure events? Also check if we got network retries to the model hosts.
Amy: No obvious autoscaler events. Grafana panels show increased queue_depth on a few hosts, but CPU/GPU metrics not OOMting.
Maria: Logs from the host pool show a burst of kube-proxy conntrack warnings + a few `X-TLS` handshake timeouts. Pasted snippet: `2025-10-12T06:13:48Z host-az3 kube-proxy conntrack: overflow`
Joel: Could be transient networking + small batch sizes causing outlier token latencies. We should confirm whether the p99 jump is real or a histogram sampling artifact.
Sanjay: Agreed. First diagnostic: compare two panels side-by-side — current p99 histogram using `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_processing_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))` vs raw `rate(token_processing_seconds_sum[5m]) / rate(token_processing_seconds_count[5m])` for mean. If the buckets are sparse the quantile will be noisy.
Amy: Reproduced query that shows bucket gaps. Here's a quick PromQL I ran: ```histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket{region="eu-west-1",model=~"gpt.*"}[10m])) by (le, shard))``` It spikes when `count` drops < ~200 samples in 10m.
InfraOncallBot: Alert: per-token-p99-eu-west-1 firing on instance pool-az3 (p99 > 500ms for 5m). Incident ticket #INC-3821 created.
Maria: Looking at NIC error counters on pool-az3: `if_errors_total` increased around same time, and retransmits on the NVLink fabric are slightly elevated. I suspect a transient networking flap that caused retries and longer tail.
Joel: For alerts we should stop relying on short-window p99. Proposal: change alert to p99 over 15m with a minimum sample filter: `count_over_time(inference_token_latency_seconds_count[15m]) > 300 and histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...[15m])) by (le, shard)) > 0.5`. That prevents alerts on low-sample noise.
Sanjay: Also add a Grafana heatmap (bucketed) panel for tokens/sec vs p99 by shard. Heatmaps make it clear when low throughput correlates with p99 jitter.
Amy: Action items: (1) Joel to draft alert update (15m + min samples), (2) Sanjay to add heatmap + side-by-side raw count panel, (3) Maria to archive NIC logs and check switch firmware for pool-az3.
Joel: I'll open a PR for the alert rule and add notes about sample floor. Example alert expr I plan to use: ```((sum by (shard) (rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_count{region="eu-west-1"}[15m])) > 20) and histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket{region="eu-west-1"}[15m])) by (le, shard)) > 0.5)``` Adjust threshold as we validate.
Maria: I've uploaded `/var/logs/host-pool-az3/nic-errors-2025-10-12.tar.gz` to the incident folder and flagged a switch vendor ticket.
Amy: One more thing — we saw a small increase in GPU queue wait_time percentiles at the same time. It might be co-contributor: small batch queues hold up KV cache access. Add those metrics to the drilldown.
Sanjay: I'll prototype a dashboard row: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, queue_depth, if_errors_total, and a bucketed histogram. Will include a toggle to filter shards with count < 50.
InfraOncallBot: Note: incident INC-3821 set to priority P3. Assigned to Maria.
Amy: Thanks — if the PR for the alert lands, let's let it run for 24h to ensure we don't lose genuine signals. If p99 re-fires with samples >300 we escalate to oncall. :thumbsup:
Sanjay: I'll add a short runbook snippet in the alert description: how to check sample count, heatmap, and nic counters. Keeps it actionable for the oncall.
Joel: PR link once ready.
Maria: Monitoring the host pool, will update if vendor responds.
Amy: Closing the loop here — good triage.
